provenance.commitSubject: AGENTS.md — the map, measured rather than remembered, and held to its sources

scenarios.name: New user completes registration and enters a usable workspace
scenarios.checks: the signup form calls supabase.auth.signUp with a confirmation redirect, and every route that redirect and its recovery paths land on is declared in the router
scenarios.notChecked: that a confirmation mail actually arrives at a real inbox — that needs the deployed origin and a third-party mailbox, neither of which exists offline

scenarios.name: Invited member joins the intended organization with correct access
scenarios.reason: organizations are not planned: the owner dispositioned three-level tenancy as not-built on 2026-09-15 (docs/design/TENANCY.md); the schema is flat (profiles -> projects) and no organizations table exists, so there is no organization to join. The equivalent capability the owner did build is per-project sharing, checked by scenario 15.

scenarios.name: Returning user resumes the correct project and conversation
scenarios.checks: the transcript route serves the owner their own project and answers a caller the row is invisible to with 404, addressing exactly one session Durable Object and only from the canonical row id
scenarios.notChecked: that a browser reload replays an in-flight run — the replay lives in the session Durable Object, which needs the Cloudflare runtime

scenarios.name: User installs the Studio plugin and pairs the intended place
scenarios.checks: place admission binds an unbound project, matches the same place, refuses a different one, and says "unverified" rather than guessing for an unsaved place — and the install link does not claim a Creator Store listing while the store flag says there is none
scenarios.notChecked: the install itself: STUDIO_PLUGIN_STORE_LIVE is false, so nobody can install this plugin from the Store, and that half of the item is unbuilt rather than untested

scenarios.name: User sees accurate connection and capability status
scenarios.checks: the client derives exactly four connection states from wire signals and has no "installed" state to invent, and its role/action mirror is identical to the worker allowlists it mirrors
scenarios.notChecked: that the rendered chrome actually shows the state it derived — that is a DOM assertion and lives in apps/web/tests

scenarios.name: User submits a request with relevant project context
scenarios.checks: the system prompt the run is built from carries the project name, the place the plugin reported, the connection state, and the memory summary and facts — and omits the memory when there is none rather than printing an empty heading
scenarios.notChecked: that the prompt reaches the provider unchanged — the send lives in the session Durable Object and needs the Cloudflare runtime

scenarios.name: Agent presents an actionable plan with visible cost expectations
scenarios.checks: a build request is restated into a checklist and open questions with no model call, and the credit cost of a run is derived from one arithmetic rather than quoted from a constant
scenarios.notChecked: that the plan is rendered beside the cost in one surface — the intent broadcast and the credit balance are produced by the worker and assembled by the client

scenarios.name: User approves the exact operations that require consent
scenarios.checks: a tool the user set to ask or deny is removed from the toolset the run may call, an allowed one is kept, and the run reports exactly which capability was withheld — and only ones it actually had
scenarios.notChecked: an in-run approval prompt for an irreversible Studio mutation: consent here is a standing setting, not a per-operation dialog, and the brief asks for both

scenarios.name: Approved operations execute against the intended Studio session
scenarios.checks: no tool that changes a place is offered while Studio is not connected, the executor refuses one anyway if it is called, and a place that does not match the binding is not served
scenarios.notChecked: that the operation reaches the paired Studio and lands — that needs a live plugin on a real place

scenarios.name: Studio changes produce persisted and inspectable results
scenarios.checks: a checkpoint is taken automatically before a builder run, and the checkpoint list is reachable by the owner and invisible to a caller the project row is invisible to
scenarios.notChecked: that generated geometry survives a save and publish round trip in Roblox Studio, and that a checkpoint can be taken at all with no plugin connected — createCheckpoint refuses without one

scenarios.name: Verification reports distinguish passed, failed, and unverified outcomes
scenarios.checks: a critique that could not be read is reported as unknown and never as a failure, a failed one says so, and a spec case that never reported is named as missing rather than counted as a pass
scenarios.notChecked: that a user ever reaches a verification — every checker requires a Studio connection

scenarios.name: User can inspect supporting evidence and operation history
scenarios.checks: the operation history route is reachable by the owner and closed to everyone else, and the partition that builds it keeps this run’s operations separate from earlier ones instead of merging them
scenarios.notChecked: that the evidence cards render the four kinds and four states — a DOM assertion, held in apps/web/tests/evidence-model.test.mjs

scenarios.name: User can reverse changes and verify restored state
scenarios.checks: a restore that skipped something is reported as a caveat rather than as a success, the fidelity line names what did not come back, and the restore route is owner-scoped
scenarios.notChecked: that Terrain and Camera actually return in Roblox Studio — that needs a live place

scenarios.name: Interrupted runs recover without duplicate writes or duplicate charges
scenarios.checks: the run guard is established before the first await, so two starts racing for the same session produce exactly one run — and the guard reopens once the run settles
scenarios.notChecked: that a dropped socket replays the transcript rather than re-running it — the replay lives in the session Durable Object

scenarios.name: Collaborators receive only the access granted to them
scenarios.checks: the role matrix refuses a viewer the actions of an editor and an editor the actions of an admin, an unreadable role is refused rather than defaulted, a share link cannot carry more than editor, and the shared route is closed to a caller with no grant
scenarios.notChecked: that the members panel is mounted anywhere a user can reach — the enforcement is proven, the surface is the brief’s open half

scenarios.name: Plan limits are enforced consistently across UI, API, and background jobs
scenarios.checks: one limits table serves the worker and the client, the quota arithmetic reads it rather than a number of its own, the tighter of the daily and monthly limits is the one that bites, and a spend takes the renewable allowance before the balance the user paid for
scenarios.notChecked: that a background automation charges the same ledger — the automation run path needs the Durable Object runtime

scenarios.name: Purchases update entitlements and credit balances accurately
scenarios.checks: entitlement is recomputed from the subscription’s status and period rather than trusted from the event, an expired period falls back to free, and a second checkout is refused while one is already active
scenarios.notChecked: that a real Stripe test-mode webhook grants entitlement — every billing route is gated on billingConfigured() (apps/worker/src/billing.ts) and this repository holds no Stripe credential, so the grant itself has never been exercised here

scenarios.name: Cancellation, downgrade, and payment failure produce documented behavior
scenarios.checks: every dunning kind the worker can raise has user-facing copy, a failure is deduplicated on the invoice so three Stripe retries are one notice, and an unrecognised event produces nothing rather than a guess
scenarios.notChecked: that the notice reaches a user — the webhook that raises it is gated on billingConfigured(), which no credential in this repository satisfies

scenarios.name: Data export and deletion complete across primary and derived storage
scenarios.checks: the export route is owner-scoped, deletion requires the typed confirmation, and the receipt names the residue deletion does NOT remove instead of claiming a completeness it does not have
scenarios.notChecked: that every derived store is actually swept on the deployed origin — the sweep runs against live KV and D1

scenarios.name: Production incidents are detected, communicated, and recoverable
scenarios.checks: every notification kind the product can raise has a spec to render it, the channels that do not exist are named as unbuilt rather than silently dropped, a scheduled handler exists and is wired to a cron trigger, and the static rollback reads back what it wrote
scenarios.notChecked: that an incident on the deployed origin is actually noticed — detection here is a daily cron, not a monitor with an alert path

measures.name: Defined analytics event catalog
measures.unit: event kinds (request, model_call, error, build, audit)
measures.how: counted from EVENT_KINDS in apps/worker/src/analytics.ts. Every one is an infrastructure event; none is a product event.

measures.name: Event schema validation
measures.because: there is no event schema to validate against. apps/worker/src/analytics.ts reads each field defensively (readNumber, readCount, readTimestamp, readText, readEnum) and refuses an unreadable one, which is field-level defence, not an event checked against a declared shape — and a count of defended fields is not a measure of schema conformance

measures.name: Registration funnel
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. Registration happens in Supabase Auth, which the worker never sees, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use

measures.name: Email verification funnel
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. Confirmation is a Supabase redirect to /confirm; nothing records the click, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use

measures.name: Onboarding completion funnel
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. Onboarding state lives in the browser (apps/web/src/lib/onboarding.ts) and is never sent anywhere

A run writes a model_call event with no per-user first-run marker, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use

measures.name: First verified change activation
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. Verification runs only with a Studio connection and records no event at all

measures.name: Trial conversion
measures.because: there is no trial to convert from: PLAN_LIMITS declares free, builder, studio, enterprise and none of them is time-limited (packages/shared/src/index.ts) — the free plan is permanent, so a trial-conversion rate is a measure of something this product does not have

measures.name: Paid conversion
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. Checkout and the Stripe webhook exist in the tree and are gated on billingConfigured() (apps/worker/src/billing.ts), which with no Stripe credential present answers false; whether the deployed origin has one is not something this report probed, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use

measures.name: Subscription retention
measures.because: retention needs a subscription table read over time, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use. Whether any subscription exists is not something this report can see

measures.name: Subscription cancellation reasons
measures.because: no cancellation reason is ever collected: the product has no cancellation survey, and the Stripe events the worker interprets (payment_failed, action_required, payment_recovered, checkout_expired) carry a status, not a reason

measures.name: Cohort retention analysis
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count, and a cohort needs a signup date the worker never sees, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use

measures.name: Feature adoption
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. Tool calls are recorded per run, not per feature per user, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use

measures.name: Collaboration adoption
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. Membership rows exist in Postgres and are readable only with a credential this report does not have

measures.name: Run success trends
measures.because: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count. A production run emits a model_call event with cost and latency and no success verdict, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use
measures.note: the nearest thing this repository can compute is the eval harness’s own success rate over packages/evals/results (`node src/score.mjs scorecard latest`). That is models against fixed tasks, not users against the product, and the two must not be quoted as each other.

measures.name: Verification success trends
measures.because: no verification outcome is recorded anywhere: no event kind names a verification (request, model_call, error, build, audit), and every tool that could produce one needs a Studio connection — 35 of 59 tools are marked studio:true and are withheld without one, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use

measures.name: Cost per successful run
measures.because: the observed cost needs per-run spend rows joined to a success verdict, and neither exists: the event catalog holds only request, model_call, error, build, audit (apps/worker/src/analytics.ts) — no signup, onboarding, pairing, conversion or retention event is emitted anywhere in the tree, so there is nothing to count, and no production datastore is reachable from this repository: Supabase, D1 and the Durable Object SQL all live behind credentials this report does not have and must not use
measures.note: from the model, not from users: a quality-gated build is priced at 77 Credits (2310 neurons, about $0.0254) by apps/worker/src/pricing.ts. That is what the arithmetic charges, not what a run has cost.

measures.name: Permission-aware internal analytics access
measures.unit: of 1 analytics read routes closed to callers without the admin key (with key 200, wrong key 403, no key 403)
measures.how: measured by driving the real Hono app from apps/worker/src/index.ts. It is a guard on a shared key, not per-person permission: there is one level of internal access, not a matrix.

measures.name: Analytics data quality monitoring
measures.unit: of 1 — every analytics metric reports {value, samples, unreadable, why}, so an unreadable batch is visible as a count rather than folded into an average
measures.how: read from apps/worker/src/analytics.ts by constructing a metric with unreadable samples. There is no alerting on it: nothing watches the unreadable count and nothing pages anybody.
